Adding source-level evidence that this is a documentation defect, rather than a tmux or Remote SSH configuration issue.

The current [IDE documentation](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/cf7503687a2485621a690d18c4b0d1ff2060bc3e/packages/web/src/content/docs/ide.mdx#L14-L15) says that the OpenCode VS Code extension will automatically share the current selection or tab.

At the same commit, the bundled `sst-dev.opencode` extension does not implement ongoing editor-context synchronization:

- It creates an `opencode` terminal, runs `opencode --port <port>`, and appends one initial `In @path` prompt: [extension.ts#L45-L101](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/cf7503687a2485621a690d18c4b0d1ff2060bc3e/sdks/vscode/src/extension.ts#L45-L101).
- It reads `activeTextEditor` only when opening that terminal or handling the explicit `Ctrl+Alt+K` command: [extension.ts#L24-L41](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/cf7503687a2485621a690d18c4b0d1ff2060bc3e/sdks/vscode/src/extension.ts#L24-L41) and [extension.ts#L103-L136](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/cf7503687a2485621a690d18c4b0d1ff2060bc3e/sdks/vscode/src/extension.ts#L103-L136).
- It does not register active-editor or selection-change listeners, create `~/.claude/ide/*.lock`, or host an editor-context WebSocket server.

OpenCode TUI does have a client for a compatible bridge. It discovers `~/.claude/ide/*.lock` files: [editor.ts#L56-L96](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/cf7503687a2485621a690d18c4b0d1ff2060bc3e/packages/tui/src/editor.ts#L56-L96), then receives `selection_changed` over WebSocket: [editor.ts#L173-L282](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/cf7503687a2485621a690d18c4b0d1ff2060bc3e/packages/tui/src/context/editor.ts#L173-L282). The OpenCode extension does not provide that bridge.

My daily setup runs OpenCode inside tmux, launched from the VS Code integrated terminal over Remote SSH. I reproduced the same result with OpenCode launched directly in a bare VS Code integrated terminal and through the OpenCode extension. tmux should not affect this behavior if the extension supplies the documented persistent editor-context bridge.

In this setup, `~/.claude/ide/` stays empty, the TUI has no active-file indicator, and switching editors or selections sends no context updates. The documentation currently describes functionality that the bundled extension does not provide.
fixed

With the current Claude Code VS Code extension, this is not an optional edge-case configuration. The extension automatically injects `CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT` into the integrated terminal environment.

That means the default setup behaves as follows:

1. The Claude Code extension creates a valid `~/.claude/ide/<port>.lock` file with an `authToken`.
2. It also exports `CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT=<port>`.
3. OpenCode prioritizes that environment variable.
4. OpenCode skips lock-file discovery and loses the `authToken`.
5. The Claude IDE bridge rejects the unauthenticated WebSocket connection.

The relevant OpenCode code gives the environment variable priority and returns only a URL, without an auth token: [resolveEditorConnection](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/cf7503687a2485621a690d18c4b0d1ff2060bc3e/packages/tui/src/context/editor.ts#L361-L374). The WebSocket client sends the Claude authorization header only when the connection contains that token: [openEditorSocket](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/cf7503687a2485621a690d18c4b0d1ff2060bc3e/packages/tui/src/context/editor.ts#L390-L398).

Therefore, installing the current Claude Code extension does not make OpenCode context awareness work by default. The user must manually remove the environment variables before launching OpenCode:

```bash
env -u CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT \
    -u OPENCODE_EDITOR_SSE_PORT \
    opencode
```

The [IDE documentation](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/cf7503687a2485621a690d18c4b0d1ff2060bc3e/packages/web/src/content/docs/ide.mdx#L14-L15) currently omits both facts: live context depends on the Claude Code extension, and the Claude Code extension default environment prevents OpenCode from authenticating to its bridge.

Confirmed on **OpenCode 1.17.20**, Windows 11, Windows Terminal / PowerShell.

A concrete reproduction is a PowerShell command executed by the OpenCode `bash` tool:

```powershell
Start-Process python `
  -ArgumentList "-m","http.server","8766" `
  -WorkingDirectory "C:\path\to\workspace" `
  -NoNewWindow
Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
Write-Output "Server started"
```

Observed behavior:

- The tool output contains `Server started\r\n`.
- The spawned Python HTTP server remains alive and responds with HTTP 200.
- The direct PowerShell work has logically completed.
- The native OpenCode tool part remains indefinitely at:

```json
{
  "tool": "bash",
  "state": {
    "status": "running",
    "metadata": {
      "output": "Server started\r\n"
    }
  }
}
```

- `GET /session/status` continues to report the OpenCode session as `busy`.
- Attaching the TUI to the same native session shows the spinner indefinitely and requires manual cancellation.

This strongly matches the inherited-pipe diagnosis in this issue: `-NoNewWindow` allows the long-lived child to retain the bash tool's stdout/stderr handles, so process output is available but EOF never arrives.

The important additional evidence here is that the background process is not merely starting slowly or failing: it is healthy and serving requests while OpenCode still considers the parent tool call running.

Related newer duplicate: #36799.

- Affected session: `ses_09fa61b72ffezk4fTmfhQkRqAw`

The configured model works for regular requests. The failure appears specific to the title-agent small-model request path. Errors are not visible because the title-generation failure is swallowed by `Effect.ignore`.

Closing this. After a deeper look, the original rationale doesn't hold and the patch isn't worth the risk:

- The premise ("a full DB reload each loop iteration breaks Anthropic prompt-cache byte-identity") was already retracted in #31525: the cache is content-based, not object-identity-based, so a reload producing identical content doesn't break it.
- The only remaining angle was redundant DB I/O, but the patch as written still calls `filterCompactedEffect` (full-history re-pagination) every iteration — it only preserved JS object identity, so it saved no I/O.
- A genuine reload-skip would need to avoid re-paginating history, which is entangled with `SessionReminders` mutating shared message objects in place and with persisted-vs-in-memory `synthetic` parts (plan mode + compaction). That's a correctness-sensitive rewrite of the core prompt loop for a benefit I'd previously rated minor — poor risk/reward.

Heads up on the overlap with #36861. Both PRs touch the same cache-write fallback, but they fix different paths, and #36861 does not cover the case in #36749.

#36861 reads the counts out of `ProviderMetadata`. For a provider on `npm: "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"`, that object never carries them. In `openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts` the metadata is built as `{ [metadataKey]: {} }` plus whatever an optional `metadataExtractor` returns, and only `acceptedPredictionTokens` / `rejectedPredictionTokens` are written into it afterwards. opencode wires a `metadataExtractor` only on the github-copilot path, so for a generic openai-compatible provider `metadataUsage()` lands on an empty record and `cache.write` stays 0.

The count does survive, just not there: `convertOpenAICompatibleChatUsage` sets `cacheWrite: undefined` and passes the gateway payload through as `usage.raw`. That is what this PR reads.

I checked this rather than assumed it. Applying #36861 on its own and running the gateway scenario from #36749 against it (`usage.raw.cache_creation_input_tokens: 19426`, no provider metadata) still yields `cacheWriteInputTokens: undefined`, so `cache.write` is still 0. Its own 30 tests pass; the raw path is simply not covered.

So the two look complementary rather than duplicate. #36861 covers providers that expose cache counts through metadata and also adds cache read; this one covers the openai-compatible SDK path, where metadata has nothing to offer. They do collide textually, so whichever lands first, the other needs a rebase. Happy to rebase on top of #36861 if that one goes first.

I reproduced a narrower version of this on macOS 26.5.2 arm64, OpenCode 1.17.20 from Homebrew, running in Ghostty. The animation toggle was the dominant variable in my case.

Same PID, session, project, and remote model while the agent was active:

- animations enabled: 24-28% CPU, later reaching 43%
- animations disabled: 6-13% CPU, then 1-5%
- enabling them again returned CPU to 24-43%
- disabling them again returned it to 1-5%

The change reproduced in both directions. FFF worker threads were asleep and there was no high-CPU child process.

A macOS `sample` taken while hot included `bufferDrawTextBufferView` and `renderer.CliRenderer.prepareRenderFrameWithWriter`. The source matches the profile: OpenCode creates the renderer with `targetFps: 60`, and its spinner advances every 80ms. `opentui-spinner` calls `requestRender()` on every frame. In OpenTUI 0.4.3, that reaches `CliRenderer.loop()`, which calls `root.render()` and walks the render list.

Relevant source:

- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.17.20/packages/tui/src/component/spinner.tsx
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.17.20/packages/tui/src/app.tsx
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/v0.4.3/packages/core/src/Renderable.ts
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/v0.4.3/packages/core/src/renderer.ts

A cheap fix may be to stop animating while streaming text is already changing the screen, then start a low-rate spinner only after no output has arrived for a short period. The existing `Disable animations` toggle avoids the problem, but it is global and manual.

One concrete data point for the incoming-stream case: on macOS arm64 with OpenCode 1.17.20, toggling TUI animations changed the same active process from 24-43% CPU to 1-13%. Repeating the toggle reproduced the increase and decrease. The model was remote, and the FFF workers were asleep.

The spinner advances every 80ms and requests a render for each frame. OpenTUI then enters `root.render()` and walks the render list. I posted the measurements, sample symbols, and source links here: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/30086#issuecomment-4971445578

This does not explain every report in this thread, especially watcher and long-session cases, but it accounts for the streaming CPU on this setup.

I saw a related macOS CLI problem on OpenCode 1.17.20, with one useful distinction: my reproducible case was tied to the busy spinner, not a true idle loop.

With animations enabled, the active TUI used 24-43% CPU. Disabling animations dropped the same process to 1-13%, and toggling them back on restored the high usage. Once no busy indicator was visible, CPU settled near 1%. Details and source links: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/30086#issuecomment-4971445578

If CPU remains high after the session status is fully idle, that is probably another path. The animation toggle is still a useful discriminator for this issue.

Heads up: #36881 just merged to v2 with essentially the same terminal guard, since this was biting production today (a truncated `write` tool-input stream settled as `execution.succeeded`, details in #36766).

Two deltas from this PR's version, both driven by it landing on current v2 rather than on the provider-error removal stack:

- The guard accepts `finish` or `provider-error` as terminal. Once #36692 lands, that predicate collapses to finish-only.
- Enforcement lives inside `streamPrepared` in `makeFromTransport` rather than in `streamRequestWith`, so direct `route.streamPrepared` consumers are covered too, and it reuses the route label already computed there. There is also a provider-neutral regression in `test/adapter.test.ts`.

So this PR should rebase down to roughly the predicate simplification plus whatever the flat error union renames. Sorry for the churn, and happy to help with the rebase if useful.
